verdict.rationale: Carta documents an OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow and OAuth scopes, and states that law firms and technology partners can fetch cap table data on the company's behalf. It also says personal-finance partners can aggregate holdings that include equity data. That covers the core of delegated third-party access. Missing for 10: documentation of how granular the scopes are (what 'scoped slices' a company can grant), any explicit mention of HRIS vendors, explicit confirmation that partner access avoids admin credentials or can be revoked, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, third parties my company authorizes — law firms, HRIS vendors, wealth managers — can access scoped slices of equity data on our behalf without full admin credentials

citations.quote: Allows law firms and technology partners to fetch cap table information on behalf of the company
Allows personal finance management partners to aggregate holdings inclusive of equity data
Carta's API uses the OAuth 2.0 open specification to authorize your access to our data, and supports AUTHORIZATION_CODE and CLIENT_CREDENTIALS grant types.
Adding new OAuth scopes to your OAuth application allows you to enhance the capabilities of your integration with the Carta API platform.
